sections.label: Unlicensed massage establishments increase
sections.summary: Between 2013 and 2016, Police detected a 40% increase in unlicensed massage establishments.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Between 2013 and 2016, there was a 40% increase in the number of unlicensed massage establishments detected by the Police.

sections.label: Clause 5 penalty increases
sections.summary: Clause 5 raises penalties for operating unlicensed massage establishments to a maximum fine of $10,000 or two years' imprisonment or both, and for repeat offenders to $20,000 or five years' imprisonment or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 5 of the Bill increases the penalty for operating unlicensed massage establishments to a maximum fine of $10,000 or two years’ imprisonment or both.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For repeat offenders, the punishment will increase to a maximum fine of $20,000 or five years’ imprisonment or both.

sections.label: Commissioner of Police closure orders
sections.summary: Clause 19 will empower the Commissioner of Police to issue a premises closure order.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: To address such behaviour, clause 19 will empower the Commissioner of Police to issue a premises closure order.

sections.label: Landlord terminate lease clause 29
sections.summary: If a tenant refuses to hand over possession within a month, clause 29 empowers the landlord to terminate the lease or tenancy without liability for breach of agreement with the occupier.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: If the tenant refuses to hand over possession of the premises within a month, the landlord is empowered under clause 29 to terminate the lease or tenancy without being liable for breach of agreement with the occupier.

sections.label: MHA amends massage definition
sections.summary: MHA will amend the definition of "massage" so that these activities no longer require a licence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: MHA will amend the definition of "massage" so that these activities no longer require a licence.

sections.label: Clause 11 licence suspension
sections.summary: Under clause 11, the Licensing Officer can immediately suspend a massage establishment licence when the licensee or a "relevant person" has been charged in Court for serious offences specified in the schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under clause 11, the Licensing Officer can immediately suspend a massage establishment licence when the licensee or a "relevant person" has been charged in Court for serious offences that will be specified in the schedule of the Act.

sections.label: Licence revocation after conviction
sections.summary: Under clause 12, conviction for scheduled serious offences leads the Licensing Officer to revoke the massage establishment licence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under clause 12, when the licensee or "relevant person" is subsequently convicted of the scheduled serious offences, the Licensing Officer will then proceed to revoke the massage establishment licence.

sections.label: Increased penalties for regulatory breaches
sections.summary: Penalties for regulatory breaches rise to a $5,000 maximum fine for first-time offenders and $10,000 or two years' imprisonment for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The penalty today for all regulatory breaches is a maximum fine of $1,000.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will increase the penalty for regulatory breaches to a maximum fine of $5,000 for first-time offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Repeat offenders will face a maximum fine of $10,000 or two years’ imprisonment or both.

sections.label: Massage Establishments Bill enforcement powers
sections.summary: The Bill lets Police take tougher enforcement action against errant operators while reducing regulatory burden for compliant ones, noting a 40% rise in unlicensed establishments from 2013 to 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, the Massage Establishments Bill will enable the Police to take tougher enforcement actions against errant massage establishment operators while reducing the regulatory burden for compliant operators.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier that between 2013 and 2016, there was a 40% increase in the number of unlicensed massage establishments.

sections.label: Landlords renting to unlicensed establishments
sections.summary: The Police will hold accountable landlords who knowingly rent premises to unlicensed massage establishments.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Thirdly, for landlords who knowingly rent out their premises to unlicensed massage establishments, the Police will hold them accountable.

sections.label: Bill's tougher penalties and closure orders
sections.summary: The Bill allows imprisonment up to two years, raises fines from $1,000 to $10,000, and lets the Police Commissioner issue premises closure orders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill gives the extra teeth necessary to ensure that vice activities can be clamped down swiftly and effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It is not just a fine, but there is also a possibility of imprisonment of up to two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Or even if it were just a fine meted out by the Court, the upper range has been extended from $1,000 to $10,000, or a tenfold increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Second, the Police Commissioner may issue a premises closure order.

sections.label: Hygiene regulation and increased fines
sections.summary: A Member asks how massage service hygiene is regulated, noting a 40% rise in unlicensed establishments and increased fines from $1,000 to $10,000 with up to two years' jail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As such, would the Minister kindly clarify how the hygiene of massage services is regulated?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: As the Minister has shared, since 2013, there has been about a 40% increase in unlicensed massage establishments in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: One important change is the increase in fines from $1,000 to $10,000 for businesses that offer vice-related services, as well as including the possibility of a jail term of up to two years.

sections.label: Massage establishments in residential areas
sections.summary: Only Category 1 or Exempted massage establishments may operate in residential areas, being CaseTrust-accredited, with at least $50,000 capital investment and low vice risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Currently, only massage establishments in the Massage Establishment (ME) Category 1 or those in the Exempted ME category are allowed to operate in residential areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: These are businesses which have CaseTrust accreditation, a capital investment of at least $50,000 and are seen as low risk in providing vice-related activities as they are usually reflexology centres or physiotherapy centres.

sections.label: Landlord eviction penalties
sections.summary: Landlords taking reasonable steps to evict the operator within a month are not penalised; those who do not face a $10,000 fine or up to two years' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Landlords who take “reasonable steps” to evict the operator within a month will not be penalised, while those who do not do so face a fine of $10,000 or imprisonment of up to two years.

sections.label: Licensing rules and penalties
sections.summary: The speaker supports robust licensing rules, higher penalties for unlicensed massage establishments, stronger Police levers, and reduced regulatory burden for low-risk activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is timely that a robust set of licensing rules is enacted, given the rapid growth of the massage industry.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I support the increase in penalties for unlicensed massage establishments, strengthening of the Police’s levers to take firm actions, whilst taking a calibrated approach to reducing the regulatory burden for low-risk activities.

sections.label: Limiting massage establishment numbers
sections.summary: URA and Police licensing should regulate growth of massage establishments in housing estates, and the Minister of State is urged to limit their number and trade radius.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) and the Police licensing regime should regulate the growth of such massage establishments operating in housing estates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge the Minister of State to consider limiting the number of massage establishments, how many can be set up within a particular trade radius, really limit it, do not let so many operate.

sections.label: Limiting massage operating hours
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Minister to limit operating hours to more reasonable timings, especially in housing estates, as round-the-clock hours may bring disamenities and temptations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I recognise that some individuals may like a massage as a stress-reliever after a long day at work, but round-the-clock operating hours may bring disamenities to the local community and temptations for illicit activities in the quiet of the night.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I urge the Minister to consider limiting the operating hours to more reasonable timings, especially if the massage establishments are in housing estates.

sections.label: Enforcement against unlicensed establishments
sections.summary: Robust enforcement plans must address the alarming 40% increase in unlicensed massage establishments mentioned in the Minister's speech.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Robust enforcement plans must be put in place to deal with the alarming increase of 40% in the number of unlicensed massage establishments, as mentioned in the Minister's speech.

sections.label: Unlicensed massage penalties and fines
sections.summary: Reports show unlicensed massage establishments rose 40% from 2013 to 2016, mostly involved in vice activities, and the speaker proposes fines scaled to operation size and duration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to reports from MHA, the number of unlicensed massage establishments increased by 40% from 2013 to 2016, and most of them were involved in vice activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Although the penalty will be increased to a maximum fine of $10,000 or imprisonment of two years or both, with fines for repeat offenders increasing to $20,000 or imprisonment of five years or both, I still think the penalty is not enough to deter the illegal operators, as their profits far exceed the fines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Hence, I suggest that besides the penalties, the amount of fines be commensurate with the size and duration of the operation, meaning that with more staff and customers involved and longer period of operation, the fines should increase in tandem.

sections.label: Penalties on establishments not workers
sections.summary: The proposed penalties target establishments rather than illegal workers, who are high-risk carriers of sexually transmitted diseases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The proposed penalties are on the establishments but not so much on the illegal workers who are high-risk carriers of sexually transmitted diseases.

sections.label: Exempting low-risk massage activities
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes exempting low-risk massage activities, such as manicure and pedicure salons, from requiring a licence to operate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, I welcome the move to reduce the regulatory burden for low-risk massage activities, such as manicure and pedicure salons, by exempting them from requiring a licence to operate.

sections.label: Harsher penalties for landlords
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes extending harsher penalties to landlords who knowingly lease properties to unlicensed operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, I welcome the measures for harsher penalties to be extended to landlords who knowingly lease their properties to unlicensed operators.

sections.label: Barring licences for same premises
sections.summary: The authorities should bar massage establishment licences from being granted to the same premises until at least a year after conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The authorities should bar any massage establishment licences from being granted to the same premises, until at least a year after the conviction.

sections.label: Resident impact and strict quota
sections.summary: The speaker hopes authorities consider residents' impact before granting licences and proposes a strict quota on massage establishments, especially 24-hour ones in residential zones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I hope the authorities can consider the impact on residents before granting such operating licences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I would also like to propose a strict quota on such massage establishments, especially those that operate 24 hours within a defined locality, particularly within a residential zone.

sections.label: Landlord eviction of unlicensed operators
sections.summary: The new Bill states that landlords of unlicensed massage establishments should evict the operator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The new Bill states that landlords of unlicensed massage establishments should evict the operator.

sections.label: Closure during Court proceedings
sections.summary: Massage establishments could be closed till the end of Court proceedings under clause 19, and low-risk massage establishments are exempted from licensing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: During the course of investigations, massage establishments could also be closed till the end of Court proceedings under clause 19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Only then would we be able to send a strong signal to owners and operators of such illicit massage establishments that their activities are not tolerated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Also, making a distinction between massage establishments and low-risk activity centres, like nail salons and hair removal centres, is noteworthy and removes the requirement for licensing for low-risk massage establishments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, I wish to seek clarification from the Second Minister with regard to TCM clinics offering therapeutic massage, whether they are also similarly covered under the Bill.

sections.label: Closer control of massage establishments
sections.summary: The Bill introduces provisions for closer control of massage establishments, with hope for greater impetus to shut down shady establishments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I, therefore, hope that with this renewed Bill, there will be greater impetus to shut down such shady establishments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This Bill introduces provisions for closer control of massage establishments.

sections.label: Massage establishments in Bukit Batok
sections.summary: In Bukit Batok Single Member Constituency, there are 14 massage establishments over the past year, three of which are 24-hour spas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In Bukit Batok Single Member Constituency, over the past year, there are 14 massage establishments, three of which are 24-hour spas.

sections.label: HDB shophouses running massage establishments
sections.summary: The Second Minister mentioned there are about 300 HDB shophouses where massage establishments have been running from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The hon Second Minister mentioned there are about 300 HDB shophouses where massage establishments have been running from.

sections.label: Exemption orders for curative massage
sections.summary: The Minister has issued exemption orders for premises where only curative massage is administered by a physiotherapist, TCM physician, or occupational therapist.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the present regime, the Minister has issued exemption orders with respect to premises in which only curative massage is administered personally by a physiotherapist who is a member of the Singapore Physiotherapist Association, a person who is a registered TCM physician with a practising certificate, or an occupational therapist who is a member of the Singapore Association of Occupation Therapist.

sections.label: Demerit points for licence breaches
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Ministry would consider a demerit point system for licence breaches, noting the Public Entertainment Act has a similar system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding that failure to comply with any condition of a licence is an offence, I wonder if the Ministry would consider introducing a system for awarding demerit points in respect of incidents or breaches of condition of licence which will then be taken into account for subsequent renewal or applications to operate a massage establishment at either the same or different premises?

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This would give the authorities greater control over repeated breaches by operators of massage establishments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In this regard, I note that section 15 of the Public Entertainment Act provides for a similar system.

sections.label: Landlord penalties and employment rules
sections.summary: The Bill penalises landlords who knowingly lease to unlicensed massage operators and regulates employment, including minimum age and medical health screenings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Bill will also penalise landlords who knowingly continue to lease premises to unlicensed massage establishment operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Based on my understanding of the Bill, lessors are expected to take reasonable steps to evict the tenant after conviction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The lessors will have some time to prepare as the Police will inform the lessors once their tenants are charged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Provisions in the Bill have been made to regulate employment at the massage establishments, such as the stipulation of the minimum age and the necessary medical health screenings.

sections.label: Rise in unlicensed massage establishments
sections.summary: Unlicensed massage establishments increased by 40% in the past three years, a problem that needs addressing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With a 40% increase in the number of unlicensed massage establishments in the past three years, this is clearly a problem that needs to be addressed.

sections.label: Higher fines and jail terms
sections.summary: The speaker agrees a $1,000 fine is too low and supports increasing penalties at least tenfold and introducing a jail term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Many have argued, and I agree, that a fine of $1,000 is too low to deter the operators of these massage parlours who can simply pay the fine after they are caught and set up a new place soon after.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By increasing the penalties by at least tenfold and introducing a jail term, we are sending a very strong message that we want to clamp down on these vice activities.

sections.label: Demand behind unlicensed parlours
sections.summary: The 40% increase in unlicensed massage parlours must be partly due to increasing demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The 40% increase in unlicensed massage parlours must be in part due to an increasing demand.

sections.label: Bill targets unlicensed massage parlours
sections.summary: The old Act was insufficient against non-compliant and unlicensed massage parlours used as fronts for vice, and this Bill shows the Government's commitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, I will come to the introduction of this Bill as it is clear that the old Act had been insufficient at targeting non-compliant and unlicensed massage parlours which are often used as fronts for vice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill shows the Government's commitment to ensure that massage parlours are held to the highest standards, which is a move away from previous Acts where parlours can continue to operate even when they have been fined for being non-compliant.

sections.label: Displacement of vice elsewhere
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry has long-term plans to ensure vice does not happen where it is not wanted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If this Bill serves only to push it somewhere else, does the Ministry have long-term plans to ensure that the vice does not happen where we do not want it to be?

sections.label: Sexual services raise salaries
sections.summary: The passage states that providing sexual services can increase salaries from between 100% and 500%, or even more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Providing sexual services can increase their salaries from between 100% and 500%, or even more.

sections.label: Stigma and displacement of sex workers
sections.summary: The passage states displacement is real, stigma on sex workers and manual labourers fuels discrimination and violence, and citizens should be treated equally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We also care about safety and hygiene despite being in the business.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am recounting this sharing to the House only to remind us that the displacement is real and genuine and should be looked at and considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: People could empathise with one another through their shared hardships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, now that we have progressed significantly, society writ large seems to look down and despise people who have not made it, even though they may have different backgrounds and opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The stigma on sex workers and other forms of manual labourers remains rampant and it only fuels discrimination and sometimes even violence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need to be able to treat all citizens equally and work together to create an equitable society.

sections.label: Penalties and unlicensed massage establishments
sections.summary: The passage supports stricter penalties, asks about a demerit points system for massage establishments, and asks how many unlicensed ones are detected monthly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: This is also where feedback from the surrounding community and the public plays an important part and the authorities can work in partnership with them as well.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I do support the stricter action on penalties with a tenfold increase in the fines and a longer jail term as well.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The previous summons of $1,000 and $50 per day for unlicensed massage parlour operators, as long as they continue operations, is really just a slap on the wrist, and no wonder they keep coming back again and again, and circulating in the industry, giving it a negative connotation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can I also find out if the authorities will consider a demerit points system for massage establishments, especially similar to the existing one for pubs and bars?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can the Minister also update us on the current magnitude of the problem, that is, how many unlicensed massage establishments, on average, are detected or raided per month?

sections.label: Licensing Officer considers planning considerations
sections.summary: The passage states that Clause 7(3) expressly requires the Licensing Officer to take into account URA's or HDB's planning considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Clause 7(3) of the Bill now expressly specifies that the Licensing Officer must take into account URA's or HDB's planning considerations.

sections.label: Category I licence criteria
sections.summary: The passage states Category I licence criteria include CaseTrust accreditation and a minimum capital investment of $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The more stringent criteria for Category I licence include the need to obtain CaseTrust accreditation which indicates good business practices covering areas, such as regulatory compliance, safety and hygiene, which Mr Christopher de Souza asked about, and consumer protection.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Another criterion is a minimum capital investment of $50,000, which provides some deterrence against fly-by-night operators hoping to roll over the quick profits of a massage establishment.

sections.label: Massage establishment operating hours restricted
sections.summary: Police have started restricting operating hours for massage establishments in HDB estates to 6.00 am to 11.00 pm daily.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Police have, indeed, started to restrict the operating hours for massage establishments in HDB estates, and only allow them to operate from 6.00 am to 11.00 pm daily.

sections.label: Vice-related infringements in massage establishments
sections.summary: In 2016, about 3% of licensed massage establishments in HDB premises had vice-related infringements.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2016, about 3% of licensed massage establishments in HDB premises were found to have vice-related infringements.

sections.label: Unlicensed massage establishments detected
sections.summary: In 2016, Police detected close to 300 unlicensed massage establishments, a 40% increase from 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In 2016, the Police detected close to 300 unlicensed massage establishments which we already know is a 40% increase from 2013.

sections.label: Landlord penalties and licence eligibility
sections.summary: Irresponsible landlords face fines up to $20,000 or five years' imprisonment or both if they re-offend, and convicted unlicensed operators will not be fit and proper to hold a licence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Under clause 5(4)(b), irresponsible landlords will be liable for fines up to $20,000 or five years' imprisonment or both, if they re-offend.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Given their history of non-compliance, convicted unlicensed massage establishment operators who intend to run beauty salons or health centres that offer massage services will not be considered "fit and proper" to hold a massage establishment licence.

sections.label: Offenders involved in illegal brothels
sections.summary: Over five years, about 12% of offenders caught for abetting vice activities were involved in illegal brothels in HDB flats, with managing a brothel punishable by fine up to $10,000 or five years' imprisonment or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Over the past five years, about 12% of offenders caught for abetting vice activities were involved in illegal brothels operating from HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: An offender convicted of managing a brothel under the Women’s Charter faces a fine of up to $10,000, or up to five years' imprisonment, or both.

sections.label: Prostitution not criminalised in Bill
sections.summary: Prostitution is not a crime per se and there is no intention to criminalise their actions in this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Prostitution is not a crime per se and there is no intention to criminalise their actions in this Bill.

sections.label: Cancelling passes of arrested foreigners
sections.summary: Foreign nationals arrested for vice-related activities will have their work passes or visit passes cancelled.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Foreign nationals who are arrested for vice-related activities will have their work passes or visit passes cancelled.

sections.label: Screening licence applicants' backgrounds
sections.summary: At licence application, Police screen the applicant and persons with influence over the business, rejecting the application if any relevant person is not fit and proper.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: At the point of licence application, the Police will carefully screen the background of the applicant and other persons with influence over the business.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If any relevant person is assessed to be not fit and proper, the Police will reject the licence application.

sections.label: Regular enforcement checks on massage establishments
sections.summary: The Police conduct regular enforcement checks to ensure massage establishments comply with regulations, with more than 100 enforcement actions a month.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Police conduct regular enforcement checks to ensure that massage establishments comply with the regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I shared earlier more than 100 enforcement actions a month.

sections.label: Stricter regime instead of demerit points
sections.summary: Because of Members' concerns, a stricter regime is preferred for massage establishments, where even a first infringement could lead to immediate licence revocation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: In a demerit points system, the licence infringements are less reprehensible and the offender is given several chances to avoid more serious consequences.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But because of the kinds of concerns that Members have spoken about, we actually prefer a stricter regime for massage establishments, to serve notice that even the first infringement could attract very serious consequences, such as the immediate revocation of licences.

sections.label: Exemptions for unlicensed and open-concept operators
sections.summary: Exemptions apply where the person is not personally administering treatment, or is an unlicensed, unregistered TCM practitioner, and open-concept massage establishments within visibility can also be exempted.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Not if you are not personally administering the treatment, you have got someone else doing it, or if, in fact, you call yourself a TCM practitioner but you do not have a licence, you do not have a registration with the TCM Board.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We can also exempt open-concept massage establishments where everything is within visibility.

sections.label: Licence needed for non-open-concept premises
sections.summary: If the activities do not take place in an open-concept type of premises, a licence is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If they do not take place in an open-concept type of premises, then they need to get a licence.

sections.label: Massage Establishments Bill support
sections.summary: MHA consulted spa and real estate associations and obtained their strong support for the Massage Establishments Bill's proposals.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: MHA has consulted the Spa Association Singapore, the Spa and Wellness Association of Singapore and the Real Estate Developers' Association of Singapore and obtained their strong support for the proposals under this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Massage Establishments Bill is important in ensuring that our regulatory regime continues to remain effective and relevant.

sections.label: Helping masseuses find proper work
sections.summary: MHA can work with NGOs to help masseuses who feel compelled into sexual services find proper licensed work.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When the Member said that he was happy that MHA will engage the sex workers, that itself sounds wrong.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, I should say that if there are masseuses who feel that they are compelled to provide sexual services, then I think we can work with the NGOs to give them the assurance that that is not the case.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Perhaps they are suitably qualified and they want to find proper work in licensed massage establishments, or they need to get the skills and the qualifications to move into these proper establishments, then I think that there must be ways of helping them to do so.

sections.label: Quota within trade radius
sections.summary: The Second Minister said MHA will consider licensing but was not explicit on setting a quota or limit within a trade radius.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: The Second Minister did say that MHA will consider that in the licensing, but she was not explicit on whether there will be a quota or a limit that will be set within a particular trade radius so that the HDB estate can be more diverse in shops, so that MHA does not approve every massage establishment licence that comes through as long as it is a not a problem.

sections.label: Approved employee identification
sections.summary: The Member seeks identification worn by approved employees, citing zero tolerance for vice and stricter licensing in residential areas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: The second one is that the Second Minister clarified that it is by law that the massage establishments must display their licence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
sentences.text: But my reference is actually the approved employees themselves must wear an identification to say that "I am an approved employee" because that will easily identify them and prevent those who are not approved from working illegally in that massage establishment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I have explained earlier that we have a zero-tolerance approach towards vice in massage establishments and the stricter licensing approach for massage establishments in residential areas.

sections.label: Assessing disamenities per area
sections.summary: MHA assesses potential disamenities in each area using community feedback before allowing or renewing a massage establishment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The better approach is to assess the potential disamenities in each area, taking into account the feedback from the community.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Then we decide whether to allow a new massage establishment to come in, or when the licence of an existing massage establishment is up for renewal, whether we want to continue to renew it.

sections.label: Licence holder accountability
sections.summary: The licence holder and operator must be accountable for activities within the premises.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The way in which we want to operate is that the licence holder, the operator, has to be accountable for the activities within the premises and he has to be the one that is taken to account.
